chapter: Dance halls and clubs of the 1930s
title: Hollywood Dance Hall and the Roosevelt Hotel band
summary: Hug describes bands he played in at the Hollywood Dance Hall and the Roosevelt Hotel, with their members.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Let's see. You say you heard rap once, huh? I heard rap once, that's right. Well, of course, there were a lot of good musicians and a lot of good bands. I think at the Hollywood Dance Hall on St. Claude Avenue, that open air dance hall that Shockey and Leon Primer had. That was a good spot there in those days. Back about 32, 33. Fazzola played there. I played with Boz and Scagliona. Boz and Scagliona used to make a real good team.
What would they play? Did you play both?

Well, let's see. I think Gene Meyer was playing, or Meyer Weinboy was playing alto lead. Fazz was playing third sax, I believe, in those days. And Scagliona was playing tenor, if I'm not mistaken. That was a real good band. And Joe Lloyd Cannon was playing bass. Aubrey Schlang played drums. That was a real good spot.
How did that deal work there? Who would have the band in charge? Shawkey.

Leon Primer wasn't playing. I think, in fact, when I joined the band, Primer had gotten out of it. I think at one time, Primer and Shawkey would play together. But at the time that I joined it, I think Shawkey was just playing one trumpet. No trombone.

I think Julian Lane might have played trombone in it. Of course, the trombone I think changed a couple of times, but I think Julian played one time there too. I worked one time too with a little outfit at the Roosevelt Hotel, and Harold Jaudy was the leader. Harold Jaudy played sax there, clarinet. He played, Harold played real good sax and clarinet too.

We had Marion Souter on trumpet. I think Red Bowman, I think they had two trumpets. I think we had Shilang on drums again. Von Gammon played drums in Viberhop. What do you call the name of him? Bill Wiley, Bill Wiley I think played guitar. He's not too well known, but he was more of a vocalist, I think.
That's not Henry Wiley's brother, huh?
No, no, this fellow's name was Wiley. Wiley.
Wiley, yeah. Wiley was the bass player, wasn't he?
Yeah, Bill Wiley was the bass player.
Bill Wiley was, yeah, bass player. Yeah, there's quite a number of things that, jobs and musicians that you meet and encounter in the course of 35 years, you know.
Some of them even have the same name. Exactly, you know. Yeah. Different instrument.
